extracted.intended_audience: drug applicants, sponsors, and regulatory affairs professionals interacting with FDA NDAs and ANDAs
extracted.subtask_short: FDA NDA and ANDA approval standards
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural criteria in 21 CFR Part 314 governing FDA complete response letters, applicant options, grounds for refusal of NDA/ANDA approval, characteristics of adequate and well‑controlled clinical investigations, and grounds/procedures for withdrawal of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete response letter: identification of specific deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete response letter identifies the specific deficiencies that the agency has identified in an application or abbreviated application, except as stated in paragraph (a)(3) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter must describe deficiencies; exception where agency issues letter without prior inspections/review if data inadequate (see paragraph (a)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete response letter: complete review of data
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete response letter reflects FDA's complete review of the data submitted in an original application or abbreviated application (or, where appropriate, a resubmission) and any amendments that the agency has reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter will identify any amendments that the agency has not yet reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete response letter: inadequate data may preclude inspections/label review
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA determines after filing that the submitted data are inadequate to support approval, the agency might issue a complete response letter without first conducting required inspections and/or reviewing proposed product labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency can issue complete response based on data inadequacy alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete response letter: recommend actions for approval when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, a complete response letter will recommend actions that the applicant might take to place the application or abbreviated application in condition for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter may include suggested steps to address deficiencies to achieve approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant action: resubmission after complete response
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving a complete response letter, the applicant may resubmit the application or abbreviated application, addressing all deficiencies identified in the complete response letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmissions are classified (Class 1/Class 2) and each class triggers a new review cycle of specified length (see subpoints i–v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission review-cycle timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 1 resubmission of an application/efficacy supplement starts a new 2-month review cycle; Class 2 starts a new 6-month review cycle; other supplement resubmissions and major/minor resubmissions of abbreviated applications start review cycles of specified lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subclauses (i)–(v) tie resubmission class/type to the length of the new review cycle beginning on FDA receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant action: withdrawal after complete response
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving a complete response letter, the applicant may withdraw the application or abbreviated application; withdrawal is without prejudice to a subsequent submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written withdrawal constitutes the applicant's request and waives other specified opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant action: request opportunity for hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request a hearing on whether there are grounds for denying approval under section 505(d) or (j)(4) of the Act; request must be submitted to the Associate Director for Policy, CDER, at the specified address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will, within 60 days or other agreed period, either approve or refuse to approve and give written notice of hearing opportunity per specified sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to take action may be deemed withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may consider an applicant's failure to take required actions within 1 year after issuance of a complete response letter to be a request by the applicant to withdraw the application, unless an extension to resubmit is requested and granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will grant any reasonable request for extension; failure to respond to withdrawal notification within 30 days results in deemed withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when FDA considers failure to act a withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA considers failure to act a request to withdraw, the agency will notify the applicant in writing; applicant has 30 days to explain why application should not be withdrawn and to request extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will grant any reasonable extension; no response within 30 days leads to deemed withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated application relying on listed drug withdrawn from market must include petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An ANDA that refers to, or a 505(j)(2)(C) petition that relies on, a listed drug that has been voluntarily withdrawn from sale in the U.S. must be accompanied by a petition seeking a determination whether the listed drug was withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons, submitted under §§10.25(a) and 10.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must contain all evidence available to the petitioner concerning reasons for withdrawal from sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA will consider evidence to determine why listed drug withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: When such a petition is submitted, the agency will consider the evidence in the petition and any other evidence before the agency and determine whether the listed drug is withdrawn from sale for safety or effectiveness reasons in accordance with procedures in §314.161.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination follows §314.161 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disapproval if listed drug withdrawn for safety/effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: An ANDA or 505(j)(2)(C) petition relying on a listed drug voluntarily withdrawn from sale will be disapproved unless the agency determines that the withdrawal was not for safety or effectiveness reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency determination controls approval/disapproval under referenced sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing to approve an NDA: inadequate manufacturing methods/facilities/controls
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may refuse to approve an NDA if the methods to be used in, and the facilities and controls used for, the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of the drug substance or product are inadequate to preserve its identity, strength, quality, purity, stability, and bioavailability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both methods and facilities; ties to product identity and quality attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: inadequate investigations/tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal may be based on investigations not including adequate tests by all methods reasonably applicable to show whether the drug is safe under proposed labeling conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates comprehensiveness of safety testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: tests show drug unsafe
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may refuse approval if results of tests show the drug is unsafe under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in its proposed labeling, or results do not show that the drug product is safe under those conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct test evidence of safety is required for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: insufficient information to determine safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal may be based on lack of sufficient information about the drug to determine whether the product is safe for use under the proposed labeling conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad criterion for data gaps on safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: lack of substantial evidence of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may refuse approval if there is a lack of substantial evidence consisting of adequate and well-controlled investigations (as defined in §314.126) that the drug will have the effect it purports or is represented to have under the proposed conditions of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References §314.126 characteristics as the standard for substantial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: proposed labeling false or misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal may be based on proposed labeling that is false or misleading in any particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling accuracy and truthfulness are grounds for refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: untrue statement of material fact in NDA
rubrics_metrics.description: If the NDA contains an untrue statement of material fact, FDA may refuse to approve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material misstatements in the application can trigger refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: labeling noncompliant with part 201
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA may be refused if the drug product's proposed labeling does not comply with requirements for labels and labeling in part 201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conformity with part 201 labeling requirements is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: missing bioavailability or bioequivalence data (part 320)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal may be based on the NDA not containing bioavailability or bioequivalence data required under part 320 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant when bioavailability/bioequivalence data are required for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: uncorrected reason from refusal-to-file letter
rubrics_metrics.description: A reason given in a letter refusing to file the NDA under §314.101(d), if the deficiency is not corrected, is a ground for refusal to approve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must correct prior refuse-to-file deficiencies to proceed to approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: manufacture in unregistered establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may refuse approval if the drug will be manufactured in whole or in part in an establishment that is not registered and not exempt from registration under section 510 and part 207.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration of manufacturing establishment is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: failure to permit inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal may result if the applicant does not permit a properly authorized HHS officer or employee an adequate opportunity to inspect facilities, controls, and records relevant to the NDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation with inspections is required for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: noncompliance with current good manufacturing practice (cGMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may refuse approval if the methods, facilities, or controls do not comply with cGMP regulations in parts 210 and 211.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with cGMP parts 210/211 is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: lack of explanation for omission of investigations or information
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA must contain an explanation of the omission of any report of an investigation of the drug product sponsored by the applicant, or an explanation of omission of other information about the drug pertinent to evaluation that the applicant received from any source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about omitted data is required; failure to explain may be grounds for refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: essential nonclinical lab study not GLP-compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonclinical laboratory study described in the NDA that is essential to show safety was not conducted in compliance with GLP regulations in part 58 and no reason for noncompliance is provided or differences do not support validity, FDA may refuse approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GLP compliance is required for essential nonclinical studies or an acceptable justification supporting validity must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: clinical investigations noncompliant with IRB/informed consent regs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any clinical investigation involving human subjects described in the NDA that was not conducted in compliance with institutional review board regulations in part 56 or informed consent regulations in part 50, such that the rights or safety of human subjects were not adequately protected, can be a ground for refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection of human subjects under parts 50 and 56 is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: refusal to permit inspection or submit reserve samples for BA/BE studies
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant or CRO that conducted a BA/BE study described in the NDA refuses to permit inspection of facilities or records or refuses to submit reserve samples when requested by FDA, approval may be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection cooperation and reserve samples for BA/BE studies are enforceable requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: failure to contain required patent information
rubrics_metrics.description: For a new drug, the NDA failed to contain the patent information required by section 505(b)(1) of the Act can be a ground for refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent information submission timelines and content per statute must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: 505(b)(2) patent certification/statement deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: A 505(b)(2) application that failed to contain a patent certification or statement with respect to each listed patent for a drug product approved in an NDA that is pharmaceutically equivalent or was approved before the 505(b)(2) application was submitted may be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific patent certifications/statements are required for 505(b)(2) filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing NDA: failure to meet nonprescription additional condition requirements (§314.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an NDA for a nonprescription drug product with an additional condition for nonprescription use under §314.56, FDA may refuse approval if the application failed to meet the §314.56 requirements applicable to NDAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional nonprescription-use requirements in §314.56 must be satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and well-controlled studies: clear statement of objectives and analysis methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Study must have a clear statement of objectives and a summary of proposed or actual methods of analysis in the protocol and report; protocol should describe proposed methods of analysis and the report should describe methods actually used or rationale if different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If protocol lacks proposed methods of analysis, the study report must explain how methods used were selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and well-controlled studies: design permitting valid comparison with a control
rubrics_metrics.description: Study design must permit a valid comparison with a control to provide a quantitative assessment of drug effect; protocol and report should describe design precisely (duration, parallel/sequential/crossover, sample size planning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognized control types: placebo concurrent control; dose-comparison concurrent control; no treatment concurrent control; active treatment concurrent control; historical control. Randomization and blinding usually expected; special analysis needed for similarity trials and historical controls reserved for special circumstances (e.g., high predictable mortality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and well-controlled studies: subject selection ensures disease/susceptibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of selection of subjects must provide adequate assurance that they have the disease/condition being studied, or evidence of susceptibility/exposure for prophylaxis studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion/exclusion criteria and diagnostic ascertainment should be appropriate and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and well-controlled studies: assignment minimizes bias and assures comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment of patients to treatment and control groups must minimize bias and assure comparability with respect to pertinent variables (age, sex, severity, duration, concomitant therapy); protocol and report should describe assignment method, ordinarily by randomization with or without stratification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomization is the ordinary standard for concurrently controlled studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and well-controlled studies: measures to minimize bias (blinding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate measures must be taken to minimize bias by subjects, observers, and analysts; protocol and report should describe procedures used such as blinding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinding of patients and/or investigators is usually expected where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and well-controlled studies: well-defined, reliable outcome assessment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of assessment of subjects' response must be well-defined and reliable; protocol and report should explain variables measured, methods of observation, and criteria to assess response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoint definitions, measurement instruments, and assessment timing should be specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and well-controlled studies: adequate analysis of results
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be an analysis adequate to assess drug effects; the study report should describe results and analytic methods including appropriate statistical methods and assessment of comparability and effects of any interim analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic methods should address comparability of groups and implications of interim looks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of §314.126 criteria by CDER Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of CDER may waive in whole or part any of the criteria in paragraph (b) with respect to a specific clinical investigation, either prior to the investigation or in evaluation of a completed study upon petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must clearly set forth specific criteria for waiver sought, why criteria not reasonably applicable, alternative procedures employed, results obtained, and why the investigations still yield substantial evidence of effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization of test drug for significance of investigation results
rubrics_metrics.description: For an investigation to be considered adequate for approval, the test drug must be standardized as to identity, strength, quality, purity, and dosage form to give significance to results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardization supports interpretability and reproducibility of study findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncontrolled/partially controlled studies not acceptable as sole basis for approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncontrolled or partially controlled studies are not acceptable as the sole basis for approval of claims of effectiveness; they may provide corroborative support or safety data and will be considered on merits except for the control-comparison requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolated case reports, random experience, or reports lacking evaluative details will not be considered as primary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing to approve an ANDA: inadequate manufacturing methods/facilities/controls
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will refuse to approve an ANDA if the methods used in, or the facilities and controls used for, the manufacture, processing, and packing of the drug product are inadequate to ensure and preserve its identity, strength, quality, and purity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels NDA manufacturing adequacy requirement for ANDAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: insufficient information on approved conditions of use of listed drug
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal may be based on information submitted with the ANDA being insufficient to show that each proposed condition of use has been previously approved for the listed drug referred to in the ANDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANDA must demonstrate that proposed uses correspond to listed drug approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: active ingredient mismatch (single-ingredient listed drug)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference listed drug has only one active ingredient and ANDA info is insufficient to show that the active ingredient is the same as that of the reference listed drug, FDA may refuse approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chemical/pharmacological identity of active ingredient must be demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: active ingredient mismatch (multiple ingredients) or different active ingredient without petition
rubrics_metrics.description: For reference listed drugs with multiple active ingredients, ANDA must show proposed active ingredients are the same; if ANDA has a different active ingredient, it must be an active ingredient of a listed drug or approved via petition under §314.93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different active ingredient requires approved petition under §314.93.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: route of administration/dosage form/strength differences without approved petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If ANDA purports same route/dosage/strength, submitted info must show sameness; if different, no approved petition under §314.93 means refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Route/form/strength sameness must be demonstrated or an approved petition must exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: failure to include petition-required information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ANDA was submitted under approval of a petition under §314.93, the ANDA must contain the information required by FDA with respect to the active ingredient, route, dosage form, or strength that differs; absence is grounds for refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow petition conditions when relying on §314.93 approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: insufficient evidence of bioequivalence or therapeutic equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in the ANDA is insufficient to show that the drug product is bioequivalent to the listed drug, or, for ANDAs submitted under petition, insufficient to show active ingredients are of same pharmacological/therapeutic class and expected to have same therapeutic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bioequivalence determinations under part 320 and petition‑specific showing required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: labeling differences render product less safe/effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is insufficient to show proposed labeling is the same as the listed drug's labeling except for allowed differences; differences must not render proposed product less safe or effective for remaining nonprotected conditions of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling parity is required except for petition-approved or patent/exclusivity-protected differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: inactive ingredients or composition raise safety/efficacy questions
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will refuse to approve an ANDA if inactive ingredients or composition are unsafe or raise reasonable basis to conclude serious questions of safety or efficacy, e.g., changes that make product noncompliant with an official compendium, introduction of previously unapproved inactive ingredients (especially parenteral/ophthalmic), use of novel delivery or modified release mechanisms, significant increases in inactive ingredient content, or vehicle/base changes affecting absorption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples include changes moving product out of compendial compliance, new inactive ingredients for route of administration, delivery mechanisms never before approved, or compositional changes that affect safety/efficacy; stricter sameness rules for parenteral and ophthalmic products and allowed exceptions for preservatives/buffers with supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: approval/withdrawal/suspension status of listed drug
rubrics_metrics.description: ANDA may be refused if the listed drug has been withdrawn or suspended for statutory grounds or FDA has published notice of opportunity for hearing to withdraw approval as described in referenced sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes §314.150(a) grounds and listed-drug withdrawal determinations under §314.161.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: failure to meet other statutory requirements under section 505(j)(2)(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: ANDA will be refused if it does not meet any other requirement under section 505(j)(2)(A) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for statutory conformity beyond enumerated items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: untrue statement of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: An ANDA containing an untrue statement of material fact may be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material misrepresentations are enforceable grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: subsequent NDA approval for change described in petition
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ANDA submitted pursuant to an approved petition under §10.30 and §314.93, if an NDA has subsequently been approved for the change described in the approved petition, the ANDA may be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent NDA approvals for the same change may preclude ANDA approval under petition pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: nonprescription additional condition requirements (§314.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ANDA for a nonprescription drug product with an additional condition for nonprescription use under §314.56, FDA may refuse approval if the application failed to meet the §314.56 requirements applicable to ANDAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonprescription-use conditions must be satisfied for ANDA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusing ANDA: refusal to permit inspection or submit reserve samples for BA/BE studies
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may refuse to approve an ANDA if the applicant or CRO that conducted a BA/BE study described in the ANDA refuses to permit inspection of facilities or records relevant to the study or refuses to submit reserve samples when requested by FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection and reserve-sample cooperation is required for BA/BE studies supporting ANDAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: expedited action for imminent hazard
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will notify the applicant and, if appropriate, others and afford an opportunity for hearing on a proposal to withdraw approval if the Secretary has suspended approval on finding of imminent hazard to public health; FDA will promptly afford an expedited hearing following summary suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited procedures apply when imminent hazard is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: new clinical or scientific evidence shows drug unsafe
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may propose withdrawal if clinical or other experience, tests, or other scientific data show the drug is unsafe for use under conditions for which it was approved, or new evidence/tests by new methods evaluated with prior evidence reveal drug not shown to be safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New data or methods that change the safety assessment can trigger withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: lack of substantial evidence post-approval
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may withdraw approval if, based on new information evaluated with prior evidence, there is a lack of substantial evidence from adequate and well-controlled investigations (see §314.126) that the drug will have the effect it is purported to have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-approval evidence can undermine the substantial evidence basis for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: untrue statement of material fact in application
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may withdraw approval if the application or abbreviated application contains any untrue statement of a material fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material misstatements discovered post-approval can lead to withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: failure to submit required patent information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent information prescribed by section 505(c) of the Act was not submitted within 30 days after FDA's written notice specifying the failure, FDA may propose withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely patent information submission is required; failure can trigger withdrawal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: failure to maintain required records or make required reports
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may notify and propose withdrawal if applicant failed to establish a system for required records, or has repeatedly/deliberately failed to maintain records or make required reports under section 505(k) or 507(g) and related sections, or refused access to copying/verification of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping and reporting obligations are enforceable post-approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: inadequate methods/facilities/controls not remedied after notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If, based on new information evaluated with prior evidence, methods, facilities, and controls are inadequate to ensure identity/strength/quality/purity and were not made adequate within reasonable time after written notice, FDA may propose withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to correct identified manufacturing deficiencies in a reasonable time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: labeling false or misleading and not corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: If labeling is false or misleading based on fair evaluation of material facts, and applicant did not correct labeling within reasonable time after agency notice, FDA may propose withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label accuracy must be maintained post-approval; corrections are required when problems identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: failure to comply with notice requirements under section 510(j)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with statutorily required notice provisions under section 510(j)(2) of the Act may be a basis for withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory notification obligations must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: failure to submit BA/BE data required under part 320
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to submit bioavailability or bioequivalence data required under part 320 can be a ground for withdrawal of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required BA/BE data must be submitted even post-approval if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: unexplained omission of investigation report or other pertinent information
rubrics_metrics.description: If application does not contain an explanation of the omission of a report of any investigation sponsored by the applicant, or omission of other information pertinent to evaluation received from any source, this can be grounds for withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must explain omitted data important to evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: essential nonclinical laboratory study not GLP-compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may withdraw approval if any essential nonclinical laboratory study described in the application and necessary to show safety was not conducted in compliance with GLP regulations (part 58) and no supporting reason or validity differences were provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GLP compliance or acceptable justification is required for essential nonclinical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: clinical investigations noncompliant with IRB/informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may propose withdrawal if any clinical investigation involving human subjects described in the application was not conducted in compliance with IRB (part 56) or informed consent (part 50) regulations such that rights or safety of subjects were not adequately protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection of human subjects is a continuing requirement affecting approval status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: refusal to permit inspection or submit reserve samples for BA/BE studies
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant or CRO that conducted a BA/BE study described in the application refuses to permit inspection of facilities or records relevant to the study or refuses to submit reserve samples when requested by FDA, withdrawal may be proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection cooperation is required and can affect approved status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval: labeling for abbreviated application inconsistent with listed drug
rubrics_metrics.description: If labeling for the drug product that is the subject of the abbreviated new drug application is no longer consistent with that for the listed drug (except for specified differences due to patents, exclusivity, manufacturer differences, or approved ANDA differences), FDA may propose withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency with listed drug labeling must be maintained for ANDAs except for allowed deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal at applicant request when drug no longer marketed
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will withdraw approval if the applicant requests withdrawal because the drug is no longer being marketed, provided none of the statutory or regulatory conditions for withdrawal apply; written request for withdrawal is considered a waiver of opportunity for hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary withdrawal by applicant is acceptable if no adverse conditions apply.
